title: Phylogenomics of Plant NLR Immune Receptors to Identify Functionally Conserved Sequence Motifs
author: Toshiyuki Sakai

steps.title: Install required bioinformatics tools
steps.instruction: Download and install each software at the specified version using the provided URLs or commands; ensure a 64‑bit Linux environment (or macOS for RAxML‑NG).

substeps.instruction: InterProScan 5.53‑87.0 – download from https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/download/ and install per the site instructions.
NLRtracker v1.0.3 – download from https://github.com/slt666666/NLRtracker and install following the repository README.
NLR‑Annotator v2.1 – download from https://github.com/steuernb/NLR-Annotator and install (works without Linux).
MAFFT v7 – download from https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/ and install.

RAxML v8.2.12 – download from https://cme.h-its.org/exelixis/resource/download/NewManual.pdf and install; alternatively install RAxML‑NG v1.2.1 from https://github.com/amkozlov/raxml-ng?tab=readme‑ov‑file.
BLAST+ v2.12.0 – download from https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK569861/ and install.
MCL v14‑137 – run: wget http://www.micans.org/mcl/src/mcl-14-137.tar.gz; tar -zxvf mcl-14-137.tar.gz; cd mcl-14-137; ./configure --enable‑blast; make; make install.
MEME Suite v5.5.5 – download from https://meme-suite.org/meme/doc/install.html (or use the web server at https://meme-suite.org/meme/tools/meme).
HMMER v3.4 – download from https://github.com/EddyRivasLab/hmmer and install.

steps.title: Download plant proteome protein files
steps.instruction: Obtain protein FASTA files for Arabidopsis thaliana (Araport11), Beta vulgaris (RefBeet‑1.2), Solanum lycopersicum (ITAG 2.4), Nicotiana benthamiana (v0.4.4), Oryza sativa (Release 7), and Hordeum vulgare (IBSC_v2) from the listed genome portals, then concatenate all files into a single FASTA named “NLRtracker_input_protein.fasta”.

steps.title: Annotate NLRs with NLRtracker
steps.instruction: Run NLRtracker on the compiled protein file: ./NLRtracker -s NLRtracker_input_protein.fasta -o NLRtracker_output. The resulting NLR protein sequences are saved as “NLR.fasta” inside the NLRtracker_output folder (total 1,862 NLRs).

steps.title: Create combined NLR set and align
steps.instruction: Add 31 functionally characterized CC‑NLR sequences to the NLR.fasta file, producing “NLR_set.fasta”. Align all sequences with MAFFT: mafft NLR_set.fasta > NLR_set_alignment_output.fasta.

steps.title: Extract NB‑ARC domains and clean gaps
steps.instruction: Using Supplemental script 1, extract the NB‑ARC domain region (based on Arabidopsis ZAR1) from NLR_set_alignment_output.fasta, discard any protein lacking the intact p‑loop motif (G/AxxxxGKT/S), and remove alignment gaps. Save the cleaned sequences as “NLR_set_alignment_NBARC_RemGap.fasta”.

steps.title: Build maximum‑likelihood tree with RAxML
steps.instruction: Run RAxML on the NB‑ARC alignment: raxmlHPC‑PTHREADS‑AVX2 -s NLR_set_alignment_NBARC_RemGap.fasta -n NLR_MLtree -m PROTGAMMAAUTO -f a -# 100 -x 1024 -p 121. Options –f a and –# 100 perform 100 bootstrap iterations; –x 1024 and –p 121 set random seeds.

steps.title: Identify CC‑NLR clade and extract sequences
steps.instruction: Visualize the tree file “RAxML_bipartitions.NLR_MLtree” in iTOL, select the CC‑NLR subclade (1,305 protein IDs, Dataset S6), and extract the corresponding protein sequences from NLR_set.fasta using Supplemental script 2, saving them as “CCNLR_set.fasta”.

steps.title: Extract N‑terminal domains of CC‑NLRs
steps.instruction: Align CCNLR_set.fasta with MAFFT (as in step B3), then cut each sequence at the start position of the ZAR1 NB‑ARC domain; the upstream region constitutes the N‑terminal domain. Save all N‑terminal sequences as “CCNLR_Ndomain_set.fasta”.
